text: After all this was done, the leaders came to me and said, 'The people of Israel, including the priests and Levites, have not kept themselves separate from the surrounding peoples and their detestable practices — the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites.'

'They have taken wives from among them for themselves and their sons, mixing the holy offspring with the peoples around them — and the leaders and officials have been the worst offenders in this unfaithfulness.'
When I heard this, I tore my tunic and cloak, pulled hair from my head and beard, and sat down stunned.
Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered around me because of this unfaithfulness of the returned exiles, while I sat there stunned until the evening offering.
At the time of the evening offering I got up from my humiliation, my tunic and cloak still torn, and I fell on my knees, stretching out my hands to the LORD my God,
and I prayed: 'My God, I am too ashamed and disgraced to lift my face to you, my God, because our sins are piled higher than our heads and our guilt reaches to the sky.'

'From the days of our ancestors until now we have been deep in guilt. Because of our sins, we, our kings, and our priests have been handed over to foreign kings, to the sword, to captivity, to plunder, and to public shame, just as it is today.'

'But now, for a brief moment, the LORD our God has been gracious in leaving us a surviving remnant and giving us a firm place in his holy site, so that our God might brighten our eyes and give us a little relief in our slavery.'

'We are indeed slaves, yet even in our slavery our God has not abandoned us. He has shown us kindness before the kings of Persia, giving us relief to rebuild the house of our God, restore its ruins, and provide us a protective wall in Judah and Jerusalem.'
'And now, our God, what can we say after all this? For we have abandoned the commands'

'you gave through your servants the prophets, saying: The land you are entering to take as your own is defiled by the impurity of its peoples and their detestable, unclean practices, filling it from end to end.'

'So do not give your daughters in marriage to their sons or take their daughters for your sons, and never seek their peace or prosperity — so that you may be strong, enjoy the good of the land, and pass it down to your descendants forever.'
'After everything that has come upon us because of our evil deeds and our great guilt, though you our God have punished us far less than our sins deserved and have preserved a remnant such as this,'
'should we now break your commands again by intermarrying with peoples who practice these detestable things? Would you not be angry enough to destroy us completely, leaving no remnant or survivor?'
'LORD, God of Israel, you are righteous, for we remain a rescued remnant to this day. Here we are before you in our guilt, though because of it none of us can stand in your presence.'
